design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (warranty_claims_and_transfers). Draw (draw_counts.py --task 0): prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[4,5,6] -> transfer fee 4, missed-visit fee 5, trip charge 6.
WHY A GOOD TEST: the caller only asks to confirm the transfer of his window coverage to the buyer. The transfer fee policy says the request is not placed in transfer pending until every billable technician visit carries its trip charge; the records show the repaired visit of 2026-10-03 (outside the 5-year labor term) has labor but no trip entry. The trip policy says the trip of a visit that rebooks a chargeable missed visit is fixed only after that missed visit's no-show fee entry stands; the 2026-09-19 no-show has none. So the agent must bill the no-show fee, then the trip net of the missed-visit credit, then hand the confirmation to the seller with the fee. Difficulty = discovering the chain from two state-form prerequisite sentences plus three multi-factor computations over the warranty ledger, the CareLine plan and its service calls, the installation job and its fees, the factory build class and the window contract.
SCOPE: first task; claims warranty_ext_missed_visit_fee, warranty_ext_visit_trip_billing, warranty_ext_transfer_fee_confirmation and their tools. Left for task 1: labor billing of a visit and the owner's acceptance of a prorated seal-failure share (labor and prorated_parts_share charges), a disjoint core.
PROBLEM TREE: transfer (user, root) <-state_gate- trip (agent) <-value_input- missed-visit fee (agent). Edge 1 sentence (negated direction): 'A transfer request is not placed in transfer pending, and its fee is not charged, until every completed technician visit on the registration that the warranty terms bill a trip charge for carries its trip charge entry on the warranty charges of the registration.' Only the trip policy writes trip_charge entries. Edge 2 sentence (affirmative): 'The trip charge of a visit that rebooks a chargeable missed visit on the same claim is fixed only after the records carry the no-show fee entry for that missed visit.' Only the missed-visit policy writes no_show_fee entries. Both false at the opening (rows a12/a13 and a11/a10 in prerequisite_closure). Deletion sensitivity: skipping the no-show fee makes the trip 209.25 instead of 24.87; skipping the trip leaves no trip row. value_input edges = 1 >= max(2-1,1).
BASE-INVARIANT CARD: every write's subject is warranty_charge_assessed; the governing base policies (agg_claims_per_registration, glass_breakage, proration, service_charges, transfer) carry no eligibility gate on that event, so each is policy_scope. The transfer's own base gates (transferable_plan: Lifetime Limited is transferable, transfer_count 0 < 1; transfer_window: closing 2026-10-09, confirmation 2026-10-16 = 7 calendar days counted from the day after closing, within 30, inclusive; a confirmation on 2026-11-08 would be the last accepted day, 2026-11-09 refused) hold on the records; the subject is declared as the fee event only because the blueprint's transfer_window gate is a mixed-authority gate with a single correlation key that the solvability gate cannot bind both ways (route-around inside this difficulty).
BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD: registration WR-4318275; hardware claim filed 2026-06-01 (3 units, approved parts only). Included: no-show visits of the registration (2023-03-11 lifetime only, 2026-06-25, 2026-07-23, 2026-09-19); the 2026-10-03 visit; the 2026-09-19 fee as credit. Excluded: the 118.00 fee of 2026-07-23 (72 days before the visit, outside the 30-day credit window) and the 2023 weatherstrip claim charges.
FACTOR CARD: see computations[].factor_trace; every factor is off its fall-through (sensitivity figures recorded). Near-misses: 2023 no-show outside the member window; 2026-07-23 fee outside the credit window; repair visit 2026-08-14 counted against 0 free trips; military vs first-responder rates differ in the 3300 series (0.10 vs 0.08).
SEED: every row read by a gold find; historical charges recomputed with the same policies at their own dates (seed_consistency). Seeded service rows follow the CareLine Plus charter (plan fee 189.00, a missed tune-up on 2026-07-08 carrying no fee as the plan year's first no-show within the plan's free count of 1 (plan history, not read by any warranty factor), and trip fee 69.00 on a plan-year-1 repair visit for caulking outside every warranty term).
PERSONA: retired engineer, short sentences; volunteers only the sale, the form and the wish to confirm today; identity, registration number, buyer and CareLine membership only when asked; agrees passively to any settling the agent explains; runs the confirmation with the fee the agent gives; closes when told the transfer is pending.
STANDARD SOLUTION: locate/verify -> read registration, transfer request, claims, activities, window contract, factory order, install job and its activities, service plan and calls -> bill 184.38 no-show fee (2026-09-19) -> bill 24.87 trip (2026-10-03) -> hand over confirmation with fee 27.71.
VERIFICATION: /tmp scratch evaluator built on check_compute.build_env/eval_compute reproduced 184.38, 24.87 (209.25 without the fee), 27.71 and every factor_sensitivity figure; gates per task recorded below.
ROUNDS 2-3 (history, current state described in ROUND 4): round 2 relabelled counting_window as a parameter and added a method fee basis, made every rule and result round half up to the cent (true half up in compute), aligned the trip edge's condition with its sentence, and dropped the false multi-source tag on careline_member_rate; round 3 defined a CareLine plan as any plan other than the On-Call Service Account in every rule that names one, and restated the transfer month count. Round-2/3 devices later withdrawn: the CareLine free no-show draw and zero-amount charge entries.
ROUND 4 REWORK (policy re-audit revision 3): supersedes the round-2/3 notes on the free no-show tier and on zero entries. R3-O1/R3-O2 -> the missed-visit fee basis no longer draws CareLine free no-shows: its method tiers are the lower of the CareLine plan's and the warranty plan's no-show fees for a CareLine member past the waiting period, the On-Call fee for an On-Call holder, and the warranty fee otherwise; no zero-amount charge row is ever booked (a chargeable missed visit or a trip whose amount works out to zero books nothing and owes no entry), and both prerequisite sentences now wait on the entry owed, a zero amount owing none. R3-G1 -> the transfer rule's month count now follows the base anniversary convention (a missing day falls back to the last day of the month) in rule and compute (calendar arithmetic from the coverage start and confirmation dates). On this world (start 2017-11-18, confirmation 2026-10-16) 106 whole months elapse under either convention; 184.38, 24.87 and 27.71 are unchanged, and task_tools.py docstrings for the no-show and trip amounts read positive again.
GATES (round 4 final run, 2026-10-13): EXTENDED OK; TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK; REPLAY OK (closures 30/30, 28/28); SOLVABILITY OK; COMPUTE OK (branches mean 77.00, steps mean 17.00, history_rows_max 15, branches_max 80); GROUNDING OK; TRACEABILITY OK; SCOPE OK.
user_scenario: You are Douglas Sorensen, sixty, a retired civil engineer who just sold his house at 441 Kenwick Road, Upper Arlington. You talk in short, organised sentences and like to know what is being done before it is done. The sale closed on Friday, October 9, 2026. On Monday evening you filled in Ridgeline's online form to pass the window warranty on to the buyer, and the confirmation email said the registered owner has to confirm the transfer by phone, so you are calling to get the warranty transferred to the buyer today. You open with that: you sold the house, you sent in the transfer form for the window warranty, and you want to pass the window warranty on to the buyer and confirm the transfer now. Only when the agent asks you to identify yourself do you give your phone number, 6145550172, and then your email, dsorensen84@gmail.com; if a third detail is wanted you give your ZIP code, 43221, or your date of birth, February 11, 1966. If the agent asks for the warranty registration number you read it off your certificate: WR-4318275. If asked about the buyer you say the buyer is Marcy Tillotson, email marcy.tillotson4@gmail.com, and the closing date on the closing papers is October 9, 2026. If the agent asks whether you have a CareLine service plan you say yes, you signed up for the CareLine Plus plan this past May. You do not know how any warranty fee is worked out and you do not suggest one. If the agent explains that something on your warranty account has to be settled or billed before the transfer can go through, you say that is fine and that they may take care of it for you, and you let them do it; you never raise any such item yourself. Once the agent tells you the transfer confirmation is a step you must take yourself and hands it to you with the fee they have worked out, you carry out that confirmation with exactly the details and fee the agent gives you. If the agent quotes a fee you simply accept it. When the agent tells you the transfer is recorded and pending, you thank them and end the call; you ask for nothing else.

edges.condition: Every completed technician visit on the registration that the warranty terms bill a trip charge for has a trip charge entry on the claim dated with the date of that visit, unless its trip charge works out to zero.
edges.policy_source: A transfer request is not placed in transfer pending, and its fee is not charged, until every completed technician visit on the registration that the warranty terms bill a trip charge for carries its trip charge entry on the warranty charges of the registration, a visit whose trip charge works out to zero owing none.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The repaired visit of 2026-10-03 (outside the 5-year labor term, so the terms bill a trip for it) has a labor charge entry but no trip charge entry on the hardware claim.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 15 books a trip_charge entry dated 2026-10-03 on the claim; every billable visit then carries its trip charge.

edges.condition: The warranty charges of the registration carry a no-show fee entry on the claim dated with the date of the chargeable missed visit on the same claim that the visit being billed rebooks, unless that missed visit's fee works out to zero.
edges.policy_source: The trip charge of a visit that rebooks a chargeable missed visit on the same claim is fixed only after the records carry the no-show fee entry owed for that missed visit, a missed visit whose fee works out to zero owing none.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The missed visit of 2026-09-19 is chargeable (third no-show in the member window, free count 1) but no no_show_fee entry is dated 2026-09-19; the only fee entry is dated 2026-07-23.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 13 books a no_show_fee entry of 184.38 dated 2026-09-19; the trip's missed-visit credit becomes 184.38 instead of 0.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain (transfer <- trip <- no-show fee), so the order is pinned by the two prerequisite sentences; there are no parallel prerequisites.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping step 15 leaves the 2026-10-03 visit without a trip_charge entry: the terminal warranty_activities lack the 24.87 trip row (state gate; the fee itself is unchanged at 27.71).
Skipping step 13 leaves missed_visit_credit at 0.0, so the trip charge recomputes to 209.25 instead of 24.87, and the 184.38 no-show row is missing.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario mentions only selling the house, the online transfer form and confirming the transfer; it never mentions missed visits, no-show fees, trip charges or visits, and only agrees passively after the agent explains that something must be settled first.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: confirm_coverage_transfer_ce1107bd and bill_visit_trip_5cd049ac read no charge entries and never refuse: they write the registration status / charge row with the arguments given, so calling them early simply books values the policies do not support.
